dedupe_keys.name: documenting marshall and hot springs north carolina following hurricane helene

description: Documenting Marshall and Hot Springs, North Carolina, following Hurricane Helene is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Lara Maalouf, Pennsylvania State University (psu.edu). Marshall and Hot Springs, North Carolina, sustained significant damage from Hurricane Helene in September 2024. These communities are characterized by a concentration of unreinforced masonry (URM) heritage structures, making them particularly vulnerable to flood and wind loading and raising critical questions about the performance and recovery of historic built environments under extreme climate hazards. Coverage: Marshall, NC, Hot Springs, NC. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: post-hurricane recovery, Hurricane Helene, heritage structures, unreinforced masonry, flood damage, geospatial data. Published 2026-05-21. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
